problem_addressed.summary: Feature NAMES are the one attribute of the feature layer not bound to ontology identity. Formula math (fm_resolve/FORMULA_REGISTRY) and indicator periods (feature_pipeline config, CLAUDE.md 6.5 exception) are identity-bound; CANONICAL_FEATURES is a hand-written literal that the ontology's lineage.vector_key only mirrors, and ~575 production src/ call sites read canonical names by string literal in ~60 files. This is why an agreed 22-name rename touches ~5,900 tracked sites instead of one registry edit.
problem_addressed.measured_cost: Of 5,895 quoted-key sites across git-tracked src/tests/scripts/configs plus 4 model registries: 2,800 in one generated fixture (tests/fixtures/test_vectors.json, regenerable), 308 in model feature_order name lists (script-remappable), ~2,787 hand edits (scripts ~1,190, hand-written tests ~822, src/research 184, production src/ ~575 in ~60 files, configs ~19). results/ was never scanned (likely larger). Several high-count names are homonyms of DIFFERENT quantities that must NOT be renamed alongside the canonical column (double_sweep = CRT episode cache key vs FM-060 rolling window; body_ratio = displacement-candle Candle property vs FM-010 current-bar composition; retest_depth/disp_strength = legacy BitNet model input names; atr = CRT engine state/local variables).

enforcement.why_generate_not_hand_sync: A hand-written tuple that the ontology 'mirrors' (checked by a test comparing the two) can drift silently if the test is weakened or skipped; a GENERATED tuple cannot drift from its own source by construction. This is the same class of fix FEATURE_ORDER_HASH itself applies one level down (detect drift by hashing, not by trusting).
enforcement.why_fm_id_not_readable_alias: User-selected (AskUserQuestion): F.FM_021 rather than F.RETEST_DEPTH. A readable alias's own NAME goes stale after a rename (the mismatch just moves into one module); an id-keyed reference has nothing that can go stale.
enforcement.base_input_identity_gap: open/high/low/close/volume were canonical vector slots 0-4 with NO ontology identity (no id, no formula, no semantics, no lineage block) -- present only as unstructured strings in the flat `base_inputs` DAG-root list. Undetected by the existing 48/48 'canonical coverage' floor (test_feature_spec_schema.py::test_canonical_coverage_is_near_complete), because that test only checks NAME PRESENCE in base_inputs, not identity completeness. This is gap G1 from the user's requested gap census; closing it is a precondition for generating CANONICAL_FEATURES from the ontology, since generation requires every canonical slot to have a lineage.vector_key.

residual_not_fixed: The 43 consumed_by: [UNKNOWN] lineage markers on the other 43 canonical identities (gap G6) -- filling them needs a consumer census, which Step 2 will produce as a side effect; filling is a separate, later program.

Value-level issues found during the gap census (retest_depth's 0.0 sentinel, the SMC distances' 0.0 'no zone' ambiguity, session/hour_of_day UTC-vs-broker-time text per F-066) -- naming/identity gaps only, not value changes, out of scope here.
